title: The gap you identified
bullets: Previous concept left the live head exposed
A washer under the head does not cover its side
Red route is illustrative, not an arc simulation
speech: You are pointing to the right unresolved feature in the previous concept. The metal screw head remains live, while the surrounding Boden is grounded. The washer insulates underneath the head, but its side still faces grounded metal across an open gap. The red line marks that reported problem location. It is an illustration, not a calculated arc path. Replacing Teflon with ceramic underneath the head alone does not address this exposed side.

title: Enclose the head, keep the metal screw
bullets: PTFE guard surrounds the side of the head
Lip extends 4 mm beyond the head in this study
Ceramic bearing washer still supports the clamp load
Guard and cap are not structural screws
speech: My proposed change is a separate insulating guard around the live head. The green guard is machinable P T F E, not a metal shield. Its wall occupies the former exposed side region and its lip extends four millimetres beyond the head in this dimensional study. The metal screw still carries tension. The ceramic bearing washer remains on its own supported seat. The guard screws into the Boden only to retain the lightweight cover; it is not part of the main clamping load path. The cap is shown removed for tool access.

title: Cover the opening and vent the cavity
bullets: Removable insulating cap covers the live head
Offset pump-out vent; no straight-through access hole
Thread forms and tolerances still need detailing
No arc-free performance or voltage rating claimed
speech: For operation, a removable P T F E cap closes the access opening. An offset vent lets this cavity pump down with the chamber. It is not a vacuum seal, and the vent has a right angle rather than a straight hole aimed at the live head. In section you can see the insulating wall and cap surrounding the metal. This is a practical geometry to develop, not proof that arcing is eliminated. Surface flashover and deposited conductive coatings can still matter. Final dimensions require the operating gas pressure, peak R F voltage and D C bias, plus thread, thermal and prototype checks.
